title: XOR.DDoS_Botnet_Investigation_110
description: Investigate and identify the source of unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation, which are indicative of a potential XOR.DDoS botnet infection. The XOR.DDoS botnet is known for its ability to generate significant network traffic, leading to performance degradation and potential service disruption. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues. This training will guide you through identifying suspicious services, investigating network traffic, and analyzing persistence mechanisms to mitigate the threat. You will encounter flags related to systemd services and timers.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host?
levels.solution: Check the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon.service`. Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to investigate further.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Start by understanding that suspicious services often have unusual names or recent creation dates. Focus on services that might be related to network communication. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: Command Guidance
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. Look for any services that seem out of place or were recently created. Use the command `systemctl status <service-name>` to investigate further.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon.service`. Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to investigate further.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the abnormal network traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service is likely named `bot-flood.service`. Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to investigate further.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Focus on services that might be generating high volumes of network traffic. These services often have names related to flooding or network activity. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: Command Guidance
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. Look for any services that seem to be generating excessive network traffic. Use the command `systemctl status <service-name>` to investigate further.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service responsible for generating abnormal network traffic is likely named `bot-flood.service`. Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to investigate further.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers using the command `systemctl list-timers` and look for any timers that might be related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is likely named `system-update-checker.timer`. Use the command `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to investigate further.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve timers or cron jobs that start services automatically. Focus on systemd timers that might be related to the suspicious service. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

hints.title: Command Guidance
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. Look for any timers that seem to be related to the suspicious service. Use the command `systemctl status <timer-name>` to investigate further.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely named `system-update-checker.timer`. Use the command `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to investigate further.
